question.question: Can a removed node retained as leader with StepDownOnRemoval=false use the singleton safe-read shortcut when the only active voter is a different node, releasing a ReadState without fresh support?
question.importance: Local role and voter eligibility can diverge after removal. Treating another-node singleton as local authority can export a read barrier without current quorum support; actual client stale-read consequences are not established here.
contexts: Committed removal from two voters to the other sole voter
Continued public RawNode ReadIndex calls after removal

obligation.description: A ReadOnlySafe request must not release a ReadState solely on the serving node local state when that node is not an eligible voter in the active singleton configuration and it has obtained no fresh support from the sole eligible voter for that request.

scope.description: Public RawNode safe-read output after locally applied committed removal leaves another node as sole voter. Continued invocation of the library API is in scope; no integration routing layer is assumed.
assumptions: Serialized calls and application of committed configuration through ApplyConfChange.
Distinct nonempty read context; static singleton configuration after removal; no lease-based reads.
StepDownOnRemoval=false is the target configuration; true is a permitted no-output control.
Caller continues using the removed RawNode rather than imposing an external shutdown policy.
excluded: Client-return linearizability, physical persistence or arbitrary crashes.
Progress guarantee for the true-option control.
A claim that every deployment continues serving removed nodes.

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe guarantees reads through quorum communication; Node/RawNode describe the returned request-specific index as a safe application barrier. A sole voter can supply local quorum authority only if it is the serving node. Config changes take effect when applied, and StepDownOnRemoval makes role demotion optional without declaring that unsafe read results are permitted. Therefore a removed node with no fresh sole-voter support cannot use only local state as safe authority. This requirement allows silence/forwarding/rejection and does not infer liveness or demand a stale client result.
grounding.applicability: At the RawNode library boundary, ReadIndex has no stated membership precondition or automatic Stop, and ApplyConfChange documentation requires applying the removal rather than forbidding later API calls. External routing that stops removed nodes is a deployment mitigation outside this scope. The check uses actual committed removal, callbacks, elections and ordered storage; it does not arbitrarily install a config.
unresolved: No external service contract is inspected; deployment consequences remain excluded.
alternatives: Enabling StepDownOnRemoval is an existing protection and will be measured as a no-output control.

associations.rationale: Safe-read quorum responsibility applies at the public API; cardinality-only shortcut is the concrete consumer of applied voter eligibility.
